newsitem.title: USA: IPO - Progenitor pricing range cut by $3.
newsitem.headline: IPO - Progenitor pricing range cut by $3.

text.p: Progenitor Inc, which filed for its initial public offering more than a year ago, saw its pricing range slashed by more than $3 Tuesday in a move that caps a series of deflating events for the company.

Progenitor, expected to price on Wednesday, filed an IPO with the Securities and Exchange Commission on June 6, 1996. At that time, underwriters Lehman Brothers posted a pricing range of $11 to $13 for the stock.
The pricing range was later cut to $10-$12, and today it went to $7-$8.
The company, which researches genes and related proteins for the development of new pharmaceuticals, postponed its IPO last August because of adverse market conditions.

Then, under a January agreement, Progenitor licensed its leptin receptor technology to Amgen Inc in return for a $500,000 licensing fee and a commitment by Amgen to buy $5.5 million of Progenitor common stock if the IPO got off the ground.
The company will offer 2.75 million units, generating $20.6 million.
